lines.text: Project time! Today you will turn one boring weekly task into a fast, safe AI routine.
Pick one task you do every week, like a sales report, a parents’ newsletter or a client reminder list.
Write every step in order and time each one with your phone stopwatch.
This gives you the “before” time to compare with later.
Mark which steps AI can draft, such as summarising, formatting or translating.
Mark where a person must decide or check, like numbers, promises and anything sent to clients.
Always remove private details before any step that uses AI.
Save the prompts from your library, a custom assistant from lesson 7, or a spreadsheet template from lesson 4.
Write a one-page routine card: step, tool, prompt, check.
Next week, you simply follow the card step by step.
Do the task the new way and time it again, including your checking time.
Present a 3-minute demo: the task, before and after times, one mistake you caught, and your responsible-use checklist.
Start with paper, not AI: write every step of your weekly task in order.
Time each step, because you cannot prove time saved without a before number.
Circle the slow, repetitive steps, because that is where AI usually helps most.
We describe our weekly task to Claude and ask where AI can help and where we must check.
The table is useful: AI drafts and writes formulas, and we check numbers and send.
But look at the tip at the end: it suggests uploading customer names and phone numbers.
That breaks our privacy rule, so we ignore it, because you set the rules, not the AI.
Now we save one reusable prompt that turns any week’s table into a five-line update.
It says use only the numbers I give, so the AI does not invent figures.
Next week, the routine is: clean, total, paste, check, send.
Measure the new way honestly, and include the time you spend checking.
Ninety minutes before and thirty-five after means fifty-five minutes saved every week.
That is your headline for the demo, along with one mistake you caught.
Great work! Let’s remember what we learned.
Now plan it, build it, test it, and share it!
